  General explanation of how the meeting is conducted:
  1. The staff report is presented by City staff.
  2. The City Art in Public Places Advisory Committee (APPAC) ask questions if necessary for
  clarification.
  3. The applicant makes a presentation to the City APPAC.
  4. Individuals speaking in favor or opposition of the project address the City APPAC.
  5. The applicant responds to project comments.
  6. City APPAC members discuss the project.
  7. City APPAC members vote on the project.
  8. The project is forwarded to the City Council for final decision (unless directed otherwise).

TO:  ART IN PUBLIC PLACES ADVISORY COMMITTEE

FROM:  BETTY DONAVANIK
  COMMUNITY & ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT DIRECTOR

BY:  JASON C. MIKAELIAN, AICP
  COMMUNITY & ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT DEPUTY
  DIRECTOR

SUBJECT:  ART NO. 01-22 – DOWNTOWN MURALS PROGRAM

LOCATION:  #1 – CITY HALL EAST, 11333 VALLEY BOULEVARD
  #2 – 36147 CENTER STREET
  #3 – TO BE DETERMINED

APPLICANT:  CITY OF EL MONTE

RECOMMENDATION:  PROVIDE COMMENTS ON THE PRESENTED MURALS

BACKGROUND

In 2006, the City of El Monte established an Art in Public Places Ordinance (the
“Ordinance”) (El Monte Municipal Code Chapter 15.07). All commercial and industrial
developments which incur project costs totaling more than $500,000 or developments
involving the new construction of four (4) or more residential dwelling units are subject to
the Ordinance. Applicants of such projects are required to acquire and install artwork in
a publicly-accessible space or in the vicinity of the project site or pay an in-lieu fee equal
to one percent (1%) of the total project cost (with a cap of $200,000).

In 2020, the City Council authorized $300,000 from the Art in Public Places Fund to initiate
the Downtown Murals Program to produce multiple murals for properties in the downtown
area (the “Program”). The City released a Request for Qualifications (RFQ) for artists to
submit portfolios for consideration. The City Council approved an “on-call” list of 25 artists
from the Western United States and Mexico.

In March 2021, the City Council approved three (3) mural designs for the Program. Earlier
this year, the Council appointed five (5) new members to the Art in Public Places Advisory
Committee (APPAC), which had been inactive since 2018. To date, none of the murals
for the Program have been implemented. Therefore, staff went back to the City Council
on August 2, 2022 to provide an update of the Program. The Council directed staff to
present the murals to the APPAC for their feedback. Moving forward, any proposed

  •  Title: Memories of El Monte

  Location: 11333 Valley Boulevard, City Hall East (breezeway area)
  Description: 100 foot long mural made up of multiple panels depicting the City’s
  history
  Projected Completion: July 2023
  Cost: $95,000

Provide comments on the presented murals.

TO:  ART IN PUBLIC PLACES ADVISORY COMMITTEE

FROM:  BETTY DONAVANIK
  COMMUNITY & ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT DIRECTOR

BY:  SAL MENDEZ, PUBLIC WORKS DIRECTOR

SUBJECT:  ART NO. 02-22 – ART DESIGN FOR AN ARTISTIC
  CROSSWALK

LOCATION:  INTERSECTION OF MAIN STREET AND
  LEXINGTON AVENUE

APPLICANT:  CITY OF EL MONTE

RECOMMENDATION:  SELECT ONE (1) DESIGN FOR APPROVAL

BACKGROUND

The SCAG Go Human Community Program reached out to City staff for authorization to
install an artistic crosswalk at one (1) of the City’s pedestrian-heavy crosswalks. Go
Human is a community-based nonprofit organization with a 30-year history of providing
effective, high quality and culturally sensitive public health education, intervention, and
policy development in the San Gabriel Valley. The organization’s goals are to reduce
traffic collisions in Southern California by making crosswalks visible and encouraging
residents to walk or bike more.

City staff occasionally receive requests from community groups to paint, or otherwise
decorate, public crosswalks within the City’s right-of-way. Proponents of this crosswalk
art believe that decorative crosswalks provide attractive aesthetic value to typically boring
street surfaces and encourage public expression of community values. Some believe that
artwork that sharply contrasts with the black asphalt pavement surface improves
intersection safety by increasing motor vehicle operator awareness. Crosswalk art in
various forms currently exists in several California cities, including Pasadena, San
Francisco, Long Beach, and West Hollywood.

Since the Federal Highway Administration’s (FHWA) guidance encourages the use of
sound engineering judgment in unique situations, it should be noted that allowing brightly
colored artwork within public crosswalks directly conflicts with the published FHWA
guidance. However, decorative and colored artwork on crosswalks has been commonly
accepted as transportation industry best practice. The CA MUTCD 2014 Rev. states that

  ART No. 02-22 – Main Street & Lexington Avenue Crosswalk
  Page 1
 colored asphalt is appropriate if it is used for aesthetic purposes and not to replace traffic
control devices (i.e. the artwork must stay within the yellow or white crosswalk stripping).

PROPOSED DESIGNS

On August 16, 2022, staff presented the project and the following three (3) designs to the
City Council for their review and approval (see Attachment 1):

  1. Silhouettes of different people in different bright colors;
  2. Books on a bookshelf; and
  3. Piano keys.

Earlier this year, the City Council appointed five (5) new members to the Art in Public
Places Advisory Committee (APPAC), which had been inactive since 2018. Therefore,
the Council directed staff to present the designs to the APPAC for their feedback and
approval.

RECOMMENDATION

Select one (1) design for approval.

ATTACHMENT

  1. Drawings of the three (3) designs.
